    12	/-!
    13	# Finite-stage descent of rank-one H1 vanishing
    14	
    15	Vanishing after extension to an arbitrary coefficient ring is witnessed by finitely many
    16	relations when the source module is finite.  This file descends those relations to a finitely
    17	generated intermediate subalgebra, then applies the result to the actual `H1` module of a pinned
    18	cocycle datum.  The resulting datum is tied to the original one by the cocycle base-change tower
    19	law.
    20	-/

    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    36	namespace RankOneFamilyCertificates
    37	
    38	/-- If a finite module becomes zero after scalar extension, it already becomes zero over a
    39	finitely generated intermediate subalgebra.
    40	
    41	The proof descends the finitely many relations `1 ⊗ generator = 0` separately using the
    42	direct-limit theorem for tensor products, then takes their finite supremum. -/
    43	theorem exists_fg_subalgebra_tensor_subsingleton
    44	    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {M : Type w}
    45	    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    46	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    47	    (hS : Subsingleton (S ⊗[R] M)) :
    48	    ∃ A : Subalgebra R S, A.FG ∧ Subsingleton (A ⊗[R] M) := by
    49	  classical
    50	  obtain ⟨n, s, hs⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin (R := R) (M := M)
    51	  let A0 : Subalgebra R S := ⊥
    52	  let t : Fin n → A0 ⊗[R] M := fun i => (1 : A0) ⊗ₜ[R] s i
    53	  have ht : ∀ i, A0.val.toLinearMap.rTensor M (t i) =
    54	      A0.val.toLinearMap.rTensor M 0 := by
    55	    intro i
    56	    exact hS.elim _ _
    57	  choose A hA0 hAfg hAzero using fun i =>
    58	    TensorProduct.Algebra.eq_of_fg_of_subtype_eq
    59	      (A := A0) Subalgebra.fg_bot (ht i)
    60	  let B : Subalgebra R S := Finset.univ.sup A
    61	  have hBfg : B.FG := by
    62	    dsimp only [B]
    63	    induction (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) using Finset.induction_on with
    64	    | empty => simpa using (Subalgebra.fg_bot : (⊥ : Subalgebra R S).FG)
    65	    | @insert a q ha ih =>
    66	        simpa [Finset.sup_insert] using (hAfg a).sup ih
    67	  have hAB : ∀ i, A i ≤ B := by
    68	    intro i
    69	    exact Finset.le_sup (s := Finset.univ) (f := A) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    70	  have hgen_zero : ∀ i, (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[R] s i = 0 := by
    71	    intro i
    72	    have hi := congrArg
    73	      ((Subalgebra.inclusion (hAB i)).toLinearMap.rTensor M) (hAzero i)
    74	    simpa [t, A0] using hi
    75	  let f : M →ₗ[R] B ⊗[R] M := (TensorProduct.mk R B M) 1
    76	  have hspan : Submodule.span R (Set.range s) ≤ LinearMap.ker f := by
    77	    rw [Submodule.span_le]
    78	    rintro m ⟨i, rfl⟩
    79	    exact hgen_zero i
    80	  have hf : f = 0 := by
    81	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_top]
    82	    exact top_unique (hs ▸ hspan)
    83	  have hone : ∀ m : M, (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[R] m = 0 := by
    84	    intro m
    85	    exact DFunLike.congr_fun hf m
    86	  have hall : ∀ z : B ⊗[R] M, z = 0 := by
    87	    intro z
    88	    induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    89	    | zero => rfl
    90	    | tmul b m =>
    91	        calc
    92	          b ⊗ₜ[R] m = b • ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[R] m) := by
    93	            rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
    94	            simp
    95	          _ = 0 := by rw [hone]; simp
    96	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
    97	  exact ⟨B, hBfg, ⟨fun x y => (hall x).trans (hall y).symm⟩⟩
    98	
    99	end RankOneFamilyCertificates

   109	
   110	/-- Tensor vanishing of the datum pair's `H1` forces `H1` of the actual base-changed datum pair
   111	to vanish.  This is the forward half of the Cech base-change dictionary over an arbitrary ring,
   112	not only over residue fields. -/
   113	theorem subsingleton_pairH1_baseChange_of_tensor
   114	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
   115	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra R A]
   116	    [IsScalarTower k R A]
   117	    (h : Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[R] A)) :
   118	    Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).H1 := by
   119	  have hcok := ((datumPair D).subsingleton_h1_rTensor_iff A).mp h
   120	  have hbc : Function.Surjective ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange A) := by
   121	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top]
   122	    exact Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp hcok
   123	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).diff :=
   124	    RigidEngine.surjective_congr _ _ (D.datumDomBaseChange A)
   125	      (D.termBaseChangeInf A) (fun x => D.datumDiffBaseChange A x) hbc
   126	  have himg : (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).imageLattice = ⊤ := by
   127	    rw [← (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).range_diff_eq, LinearMap.range_eq_top]
   128	    exact hsurj
   129	  rw [TwoLatticePair.H1, himg]
   130	  infer_instance
   131	
   132	/-- Refine a finitely generated coefficient stage until the actual datum pair has vanishing
   133	`H1`.  The refined ring is finite type over the ground field, hence Noetherian, and its datum
   134	base-changes to exactly the same datum over the ambient coefficient ring. -/
   135	theorem exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage
   136	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
   137	    (R0 : Subalgebra k S) (hR0 : R0.FG)
   138	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (R0 : Type u) pi)
   139	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   140	    (hS : Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[R0] S)) :
   141	    ∃ A : Subalgebra (R0 : Type u) S,
   142	      A.FG ∧ Algebra.FiniteType k A ∧ IsNoetherianRing A ∧
   143	        Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).H1 ∧
   144	        (D.baseChange A).baseChange S = D.baseChange S := by
   145	  letI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₀ hpi
   146	  letI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₁ hpi
   147	  letI : Module.Finite (R0 : Type u) (datumPair D).H1 :=
   148	    (datumPair D).moduleFinite_h1
   149	  have hS' : Subsingleton (S ⊗[R0] (datumPair D).H1) :=
   150	    (TensorProduct.comm (R0 : Type u) (datumPair D).H1 S).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp hS
   151	  obtain ⟨A, hAfg, hAtensor⟩ :=
   152	    RankOneFamilyCertificates.exists_fg_subalgebra_tensor_subsingleton hS'
   153	  have hAtensor' : Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[R0] A) :=
   154	    (TensorProduct.comm (R0 : Type u) (datumPair D).H1 A).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mpr
   155	      hAtensor
   156	  have hApair : Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange A)).H1 :=
   157	    D.subsingleton_pairH1_baseChange_of_tensor A hAtensor'
   158	  have hR0ft : Algebra.FiniteType k R0 :=
   159	    (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType R0).mp hR0
   160	  have hAft : Algebra.FiniteType (R0 : Type u) A :=
   161	    (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType A).mp hAfg
   162	  have hAkt : Algebra.FiniteType k A := Algebra.FiniteType.trans hR0ft hAft
   163	  letI : Algebra.FiniteType k A := hAkt
   164	  have hAnoeth : IsNoetherianRing A := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k A
   165	  exact ⟨A, hAfg, hAkt, hAnoeth, hApair,
   166	    D.baseChange_baseChange C (R0 : Type u) A S⟩
   167	
   168	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   169	
   170	end AlgebraicGeometry

    13	/-!
    14	# Rank-one certificates for the displayed arbitrary-affine datum
    15	
    16	This file removes the caller-chosen descent stage from the certificate producer.  Starting with
    17	the displayed cocycle datum, it descends that datum to a finite stage, refines the stage until
    18	the actual pair `H^1` vanishes, runs the Noetherian rigid engine only there, and transports finite
    19	projective `H^0` back to the original coefficient ring.  Stalk rank is then computed on the
    20	original datum, so the degree law is never required away from the displayed family.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	open scoped TensorProduct
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    36	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    37	
    38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    39	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    40	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    41	
    42	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    43	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    44	
    45	noncomputable local instance actualDatumOverCleft :
    46	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    47	
    48	/- Re-key the canonical field base-change package for the degree predicate. -/
    49	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) actualDatumDegreeOver
    50	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    51	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
    52	  instOverBaseChange C L
    53	
    54	noncomputable local instance actualDatumDegreeSmooth
    55	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    56	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    57	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    58

    60	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    61	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=

    63

    65	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    66	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=

    70	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :

    81	/-- Residue-field divisor witnesses for the displayed cocycle datum. -/
    82	abbrev BasicOpenCocycleDatum.ResidueH1Witness
    83	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) : Prop :=
    84	  ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
    85	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    86	
    87	/-- The fibrewise degree law for the class of the displayed cocycle datum. -/
    88	abbrev BasicOpenCocycleDatum.FibreClassDegree
    89	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
    90	  ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
    91	    [IsScalarTower k B L],
    92	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass) = (n : ℤ)

    94	namespace RankOneFamilyCertificates

    96	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
    97	-- Finite-stage refinement and its scalar-extension equivalences need a larger budget.
    98	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
    99	-- The same construction synthesizes two nontrivial scalar-tower module structures.
   100	/-- Produce all four certificates for the displayed datum over an arbitrary coefficient ring.
   101	
   102	The only H1 input is a divisor witness on each residue field.  It first gives pair-H1
   103	vanishing for the displayed datum.  A finite presentation of that datum is then refined until
   104	the same pair-H1 vanishing holds at the stage itself; the Noetherian rigid engine is used only
   105	at that stage.  Its finite-projective H0 is transported back canonically, and rank one is
   106	computed on the displayed datum from its own class-degree law. -/
   107	noncomputable def ofActualDatum
   108	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
   109	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   110	    (hW : D.ResidueH1Witness)
   111	    (hdegree : D.FibreClassDegree (genus C)) :
   112	    RankOneFamilyCertificates D := by
   113	  have hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   114	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   115	    intro p
   116	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mp (hW p)
   117	  have hpair : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 :=
   118	    by
   119	      letI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₀ hpi
   120	      letI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₁ hpi
   121	      letI : Module.Finite B (datumPair D).H1 :=
   122	        (datumPair D).moduleFinite_h1
   123	      exact
   124	        AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine.subsingleton_of_forall_subsingleton_residueField_tensor
   125	          hfib
   126	  have h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) :=
   127	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mp hpair
   128	
   129	  obtain ⟨B0, hB0fg, D0, hD0⟩ := D.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq
   130	  have hpairBase : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange (B' := B))).H1 := by
   131	    rw [hD0]
   132	    exact hpair
   133	  have htensor : Subsingleton ((datumPair D0).H1 ⊗[B0] B) :=
   134	    D0.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange B hpairBase
   135	  obtain ⟨A, _, _, hAnoeth, hpairA, hAA⟩ :=
   136	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage
   137	      (C := C) (pi := pi) B0 hB0fg D0 hpi htensor
   138	
   139	  letI : IsNoetherianRing A := hAnoeth
   140	  letI : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange A)).H1 := hpairA
   141	  have hfibA : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
   142	      Subsingleton
   143	        ((datumPair (D0.baseChange A)).H1 ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   144	    intro p
   145	    infer_instance
   146	  letI := (D0.baseChange A).moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₀ hpi
   147	  letI := (D0.baseChange A).moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₁ hpi
   148	  letI := (D0.baseChange A).projective_sections₀
   149	  letI := (D0.baseChange A).projective_sections₁
   150	  letI := (D0.baseChange A).projective_sectionsInf
   151	  letI : Module.Projective A
   152	      (((D0.baseChange A).sheaf.obj.obj
   153	          (op (relCover C A (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)) ×
   154	        ((D0.baseChange A).sheaf.obj.obj
   155	          (op (relCover C A (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁))) :=
   156	    Module.Projective.prod
   157	  obtain ⟨_, hfiniteA, hprojectiveA⟩ :=
   158	    (D0.baseChange A).pairData.rigidEngine
   159	      (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C A (fiberTwoCover pi))
   160	      (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C A (fiberTwoCover pi))
   161	      (relCover_sup C A (fiberTwoCover pi)) hfibA
   162	
   163	  have hbase : (D0.baseChange A).baseChange B = D := hAA.trans hD0
   164	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A).sheaf 0
   165	  letI : Module.Finite A Q := hfiniteA
   166	  letI : Module.Projective A Q := hprojectiveA
   167	  let e : B ⊗[A] Q ≃ₗ[B] Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 :=
   168	    ((D0.baseChange A).datumH0BaseChange B hpairA).trans
   169	      (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv
   170	        (eqToIso (congrArg
   171	          (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi => E.sheaf) hbase)) 0)
   172	  letI : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] Q) := by infer_instance
   173	  letI : Module.Projective B (B ⊗[A] Q) := by infer_instance
   174	  have hfinite : Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   175	    Module.Finite.equiv e
   176	  have hprojective : Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   177	    Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   178	  have hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   179	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   180	    D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_actualPairH1
   181	      (n := genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C) hpair hfinite hprojective hdegree
   182	  exact ⟨h1, hfinite, hprojective, hrank⟩
   183

===== presentation_struct =====
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    72	  datum_class :
    73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
    80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
    87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    90	  h0_rank_one :
    91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    93	
    94	namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    95	
    96	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    97	
    98	noncomputable local instance presentationModuleSections
    99	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) (U : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens) :
   100	    Module P.cover.Carrier Γ(P.module, U) :=
   101	  Scheme.moduleKSections
   102	    (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module U
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.
   105	
   106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
   107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   109	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   110	    B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] (Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B]
   111	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   112	  P.datum.datumH0BaseChange B
   113	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing)
   114	
   115	/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
   116	noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   117	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj

    13	# Locally constant functions
    14	
    15	This file sets up the theory of locally constant function from a topological space to a type.
    16	
    17	## Main definitions and constructions
    18	
    19	* `IsLocallyConstant f` : a map `f : X → Y` where `X` is a topological space is locally
    20	                            constant if every set in `Y` has an open preimage.
    21	* `LocallyConstant X Y` : the type of locally constant maps from `X` to `Y`
    22	* `LocallyConstant.map` : push-forward of locally constant maps
    23	* `LocallyConstant.comap` : pull-back of locally constant maps
    24	-/

    28	variable {X Y Z α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]

    30	open Set Filter

    32	
    33	/-- A function between topological spaces is locally constant if the preimage of any set is open. -/
    34	def IsLocallyConstant (f : X → Y) : Prop :=
    35	  ∀ s : Set Y, IsOpen (f ⁻¹' s)
    36	
    37	namespace IsLocallyConstant
    38	
    39	open List in
    40	protected theorem tfae (f : X → Y) :
    41	    TFAE [IsLocallyConstant f,
    42	      ∀ x, ∀ᶠ x' in 𝓝 x, f x' = f x,
    43	      ∀ x, IsOpen { x' | f x' = f x },
    44	      ∀ y, IsOpen (f ⁻¹' {y}),
    45	      ∀ x, ∃ U : Set X, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ ∀ x' ∈ U, f x' = f x] := by
    46	  tfae_have 1 → 4 := fun h y => h {y}
    47	  tfae_have 4 → 3 := fun h x => h (f x)
    48	  tfae_have 3 → 2 := fun h x => IsOpen.mem_nhds (h x) rfl
    49	  tfae_have 2 → 5
    50	  | h, x => by
    51	    rcases mem_nhds_iff.1 (h x) with ⟨U, eq, hU, hx⟩
    52	    exact ⟨U, hU, hx, eq⟩
    53	  tfae_have 5 → 1
    54	  | h, s => by
    55	    refine isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open.2 fun x hx ↦ ?_
    56	    rcases h x with ⟨U, hU, hxU, eq⟩
    57	    exact ⟨U, fun x' hx' => mem_preimage.2 <| (eq x' hx').symm ▸ hx, hU, hxU⟩
    58	  tfae_finish

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83	
    84	-- data
    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
    93	
    94	-- data
    95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
    96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    99	  sorry
   100	
   101	namespace Jacobian
   102	
   103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
   104	
   105	-- data
   106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
   107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
   108	  sorry
   109	
   110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
   111	genus of `C`. -/
   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
   116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry
   122	
   123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   126	  sorry
   127	
   128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
   129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   134	  sorry
   135	
   136	/--
   137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   140	-/
   141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   147	  sorry
   148	
   149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
   150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
   151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
   152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
   153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   156	  map _ := sorry
   157	  map_id := sorry
   158	  map_comp := sorry
   159	
   160	end Jacobian
   161	
   162	/-! ## Base change of fields
   163	
   164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
   167	
   168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
   169	-/
   170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   173	
   174	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=

    22	`quasiCompact_jacobian` (DJ-1) is landed"* and that the `rep :=` line needs **no adapter**

    27	tree: the defeq is recorded as an `example`, so nothing *consumes* it, and DAT-J's assembly

    31	writing it is what turns "DAT-G produces a datum over `k'`, and separately DAT-J wants one
    32	over `k`" into a single arrow, and it is what makes the remaining DAT-J debt *visibly* two
    33	statements (the DAT-G descent, and the quasi-compactness) rather than an unspecified
    34	assembly.

===== hgraphskill =====
---
name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

===== inboxskill =====
---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational
messages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short
bullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the
thread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely
multi-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and
are rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are
rejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave

   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.

events.text: The rank argument itself is mathematically stronger than it first appears: it does not need connectedness or surjectivity. If rank differs from one anywhere, local constancy makes that failure locus open; density of `Spec B → Spec A₀` forces an image point inside it, contradicting the transported presentation rank. The remaining risk is formal, not conceptual, so I’m tracing the exact sigma-extension and vehicle constructors needed to turn the affine choice into a natural classifier.
